title: Speed-Optimized Workflow Analyzer
idea: Build a tool that measures and benchmarks your actual AI tool response times across different providers/models, then recommends faster alternatives for your repeated tasks.
why_now: OpenAI's emphasis on inference speed as a competitive frontier means the speed gap between models is widening fast—what was acceptable last month might be slow today, and you need visibility into where you're actually losing time.
smallest: Create a Make.com workflow that logs response times for your 3 most-used AI tasks (e.g., Claude API call + GPT call + local model), stores them in a spreadsheet with timestamps, and flags when one provider consistently outperforms another by >20%.

title: Rapid-Fire Research Digest Engine
idea: Build a daily-updated knowledge base that ingests trending AI/tech headlines, extracts actionable insights, and serves them back as structured briefing cards without manual curation.
why_now: OpenAI's speed obsession signals the market moving fast—Jason needs a system that keeps pace with headlines automatically rather than falling behind.
smallest: Wire up n8n to pull 5 tech headlines hourly, send each through Claude with a prompt that extracts "Why this matters" + "Could build X with this", store results in Supabase, then display today's findings as a simple searchable table.

title: Policy Pitch Validator
idea: Build a tool that takes policy ideas and stress-tests them against real-world implementation scenarios using structured debate between multiple AI perspectives.
tool: Claude API + Gamma (for live presentation generation) + a simple backend like Flask or FastAPI
why_now: OpenAI's new funding for independent AI policy projects means there's genuine demand for tools that help people stress-test and refine policy concepts before submission or public presentation.
smallest: Create a single-prompt interface where someone pastes a policy idea, and Claude generates a 3-perspective analysis (implementation officer, skeptic, and economist) that Gamma automatically turns into a shareable slide deck.

title: Policy Idea Validator
idea: Build a tool that takes a policy proposal and stress-tests it against economic opportunity and societal resilience frameworks, surfacing blind spots and unintended consequences before public launch.
tool: Claude API + Anthropic's Batch API + a lightweight Streamlit interface
why_now: OpenAI just funded 14 independent policy projects; demonstrating rigorous vetting methodology early could attract attention from funders and position Jason as someone who understands how to validate ideas at scale.
smallest: Accept a raw policy text, run it through structured Claude prompts that interrogate job impact, equity distribution, and failure modes, return a scored assessment with specific concerns flagged.

title: Teen AI Voice Coach
idea: Build a tool that lets teens record themselves speaking about a topic, then get AI feedback on clarity, critical thinking quality, and responsible AI framing—helping them develop the "thinking critically about AI" skills OpenAI and CodeAI are pushing.
tool: Anthropic's Batch API + a lightweight FastAPI backend + basic audio transcription via Whisper, deployed on Vercel.
why_now: ChatGPT for Teens just launched with a focus on learning and critical thinking; this tool directly teaches the meta-skill of *evaluating your own AI thinking* rather than just using AI passively.
smallest: Today, build a single-page interface where a teen can paste or upload a short audio clip, get it transcribed, and receive Claude's structured feedback on three dimensions: (1) clarity of reasoning, (2) spots where they might need to fact-check or verify, (3) quality of the argument itself—all framed as coaching, not grading.
